title: granular-cooldown-policy-and-rate-pattern-anchoring
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: We observed oscillatory scale events for several mid-size tenants during diurnal traffic ramps. Root cause analysis showed the global cooldown window is too coarse relative to tenant traffic burstiness, causing over-reaction on transient spikes and unnecessary cost. This PR implements a per-tenant granular cooldown controller plus a "rate-pattern anchoring" algorithm that anchors cooldown decisions to recent percentile-backed rate patterns to reduce oscillation. The feature is gated behind a feature flag (runtime.cooldown_anchor) and defaulted off. Changes include: 1) a new autoscaler controller that computes cooldown_window_ms per-tenant using EWMA of request rates, burstiness index (p95/p50 ratio), and an anchor derived from the 95th percentile sustained rate over a sliding 15m window; 2) a cost-aware warmup stage that issues soft pre-provision requests to warm GPU pools for tenants predicted to need capacity within the next cooldown window, bounded by a per-tenant budget; 3) telemetry: expose cooldown_window_ms, anchor_rate_rps, warmup_requests_issued, and cooldown_suppression_count as top-level metrics; 4) tests and integration harness updates and an RFC-style doc in docs/rfcs. Backwards compatibility: controller can fall back to global cooldown behavior when tenant signals are missing. Impact: reduces scale flapping for churny tenants and cuts transient overprovisioning costs by deferring full scale-up until the anchor is violated. Checklist: - [x] Implementation of controller and rate-pattern anchoring - [x] Unit tests for algorithm edge cases - [x] Integration tests with simulated tenant traffic - [x] Telemetry hooks and dashboard stub - [x] Feature-flag gating and rollout plan - [x] Docs/RFC for design and tuning knobs Rollout: start with 5 pilot tenants on dedicated clusters, monitor cooldown_suppression_count and tail latency. If suppression leads to latency regressions, rollback via feature flag.
commits: init: granular cooldown controller and feature flag
algo: add rate-pattern anchoring (95th-percentile anchor) + tests
warmup: cost-aware warmup orchestration and budget checks
tests: end-to-end integration harness for cooldown behavior
changed_files: pkg/autoscaler/cooldown_controller.go - new controller implementing per-tenant EWMA + percentile anchor and hysteresis logic
pkg/autoscaler/anchor_algorithm.go - standalone logic with config knobs (anchor_window=15m, ewma_alpha=0.2, min_cooldown_ms=30000)
pkg/autoscaler/warmup_coordinator.go - soft pre-provision requests with per-tenant budget enforcement and backoff
observability/metrics_registry.yaml - register cooldown_window_ms, anchor_rate_rps, warmup_requests_issued, cooldown_suppression_count
tests/integration/cooldown_anchor_integration_test.go - simulated traffic scenarios (burst, ramp, sporadic) and assertions
deploy/featureflags/cooldown_anchor.yaml - feature flag config and default off for production
review_comments: Mei Huang: Overall idea LGTM — can you add a short note on how this interacts with warm-pool prewarming? I worry warmup coordinator could double-provision if warm-pool also warms aggressively.
Asha Patel: Good point — added budget checks and a warm-pool lease discriminator so warmup_coordinator won't request capacity that's already reserved by warm-pool. See warmup_coordinator.go commit.
Liam O'Connor: Algorithm looks reasonable. Please add a unit test for pathological spike sequences (very short high spikes separated by low traffic) to verify anchor doesn't chase noise.
Asha Patel: Added new unit test 'anchor_spike_chasing_test' that asserts anchor remains stable for spikes shorter than 10s.
Ravi Singh: CI showed a flaky integration test on first run — reran and passed, please add a retry harness for the flapping test.
Asha Patel: Added retry wrapper for the specific test and documented the flakiness in the test header.
release_notes: Introduce per-tenant granular cooldown policy and rate-pattern anchoring to reduce autoscaler oscillations. Feature is feature-flagged (runtime.cooldown_anchor) and rollout should be staged. Metrics added for observability.
